long_biography.plain_text:
Johananoff built his career around the movement and handling of industrial chemicals. In Israel, he and his brother Moshe jointly ran Gadot Chemical Tankers and Terminals, an enterprise established by their family in the late 1950s. Gadot's integrated model joined chemical trading with marine transport, terminal storage and distribution. It gave industrial customers one chain from import to delivery.

After leaving Gadot following a financial dispute with Moshe, Johananoff developed a wider international platform. By the mid-1970s he was president of Stanalchem and chief executive of the Amsterdam- and Paris-based Johananoff Group. It encompassed fourteen operating companies in twelve countries, eight chemical tankers and dockside terminals in ten locations. Educated in English schools and fluent in several languages, he moved between Israel, the Netherlands, Scotland, France and Monaco while building a cross-border network.
